title: Source writes control characters as escapes and ships binary assets nothing loads
intent: Hard negative for file.control-bytes. Terminal libraries write NUL and ESC as `\x00`/`\u001b` escapes, which are printable bytes; a legacy file with two raw ESC bytes stays under the parser's control threshold and keeps its sample; a font, an image the entrypoint requires (a bundler asset import) and a test data file are binary, but no manifest entrypoint or install script names them. None of these reads as hidden source. Samples are inert FileRecord strings.
